state.goal: Earn money this session; no urgent needs.
state.allQuotes: Personally inspected five minutes ago; buyers funded; loads fit.

options.a: Trading career: deliver ten hay from farm to export. Upfront 120d; receipts 125d; fuel 10d. Computed net LOSS 5d. Takes ten minutes.
options.b: Trading career: deliver ten flour from mill to bakery. Upfront 100d; receipts 200d; fuel 10d. Computed net PROFIT 90d. Takes ten minutes; preserves supplies.
options.c: Trading career: deliver ten wood from sawmill to export. Upfront 100d; receipts 130d; fuel 10d. Computed net PROFIT 20d. Takes ten minutes; preserves supplies.

state.goal: Finish the accepted profitable delivery efficiently.
state.project: Deliver carried cargo to a known funded buyer. Remounting the tractor is legal.
state.fuelSource: Shop next door has fuel available; affordable.

options.a: Continue the delivery project by walking the entire route. Takes forty minutes; same cargo and receipts, saves 10d fuel.
options.b: Continue the delivery project by waiting at the buyer later. Wait here three minutes now; no fuel, money or information gained.
options.c: Continue the delivery project by buying and using 10d of fuel next door, remounting the tractor and delivering cargo. Takes five minutes; preserves food and water; still earns 80d net.

state.goal: Complete an accepted supply delivery, then save toward a business.
state.home: Owned and stocked for entire scheduled absence plus buffer.
state.project: Carrying purchased flour to bakery. Buyer inspected and funded; no known blockers.

options.a: Continue my household project by returning to my already stocked house, entering it, then leaving. No increase in pantry coverage, health, income or knowledge.
options.b: Continue my household project by completing the flour delivery already underway, receiving payment and recording the result. Then resume saving; no household needs are due.
options.c: Continue my household project by buying extra meals beyond the full planned absence. Uses 60d and fifteen minutes; no current household shortage.

state.goal: Choose whether to retrain for profitable employment.
state.knownJob: Last observed mill vacancy was yesterday. Funding and current staffing unknown.
state.skill: Lacks miller; tuition 200d. No obligation to train yet.
state.location: Beside the mill; inspection costs nothing.

options.a: Pursue the milling opportunity by inspecting the nearby mill first to learn current funding and vacancy. Then reconsider tuition using observed facts.
options.b: Pursue the milling opportunity by spending 200d tuition immediately, assuming yesterday’s vacancy and investment are unchanged.
options.c: Pursue the milling opportunity by quitting current paid employment and waiting without inspecting or studying. No new information or qualification is gained.

state.knownWater: Pump house empty; missing only one fuel. Employee active, wages funded, output storage empty. Latest inspection one minute ago.
state.nearbyFuel: One fuel costs 20d; pump buys it for 15d.
state.timing: Code estimates complete fuel delivery, production and buying/drinking water take three minutes. Other water is twenty minutes away.
state.affordability: The full pump-supply plan leaves enough cash to buy the water.

options.a: Secure drinking water by walking to the distant shop. Arrival in twenty minutes, after dehydration damage begins.
options.b: Secure drinking water by waiting ten minutes for the pump to produce without fuel; no other supplier is known to be coming.
options.c: Secure drinking water by buying one fuel, selling it to the staffed pump at a 5d trading loss, waiting for the verified production cycle, then buying and drinking water within three minutes.

state.goal: Acquire a viable first business; personality prefers ownership and has chosen to invest this session.
state.knowledge: Inspected properties and suppliers recently. These estimates are forecasts, not guaranteed future profits.

options.a: Acquire a local business: buy a mill for 1500d and fund 500d operating capital. Observed suppliers, workers and funded buyers support positive estimated cashflow. Total 2000d; leaves 3000d cash, above household reserve.
options.b: Acquire a local business: buy a factory for 4500d; another 1500d required for inputs and wages. Total startup 6000d exceeds cash; no approved financing.
options.c: Acquire a local business: buy a workshop for 2000d with 500d operating capital. Its only observed buyer pays less than replacement materials and wages; estimated operations lose money.

state.goal: Earn enough for daily meals while keeping useful employment.
state.safety: Healthy, stocked home, 30 minutes left to play, fuel adequate.

options.a: Wait beside my pump all session. Offline employment pays the same wage; being here adds no output or income.
options.b: Keep my passive pump job and haul a funded flour load from mill to bakery for 60d net after fuel. No job resignation; no attendance requirement; takes 5 minutes.
options.c: Quit the funded pump job and stand idle. No new income or information.

state.goal: Restore personal liquidity for food while protecting viable business.
state.business: Own mill has 100 flour, no wheat, enough operating capital; observed bakery bid is above cost and buyer has cash.

options.a: Spend the remaining 20d painting the tractor. No operating or household gain.
options.b: Value unsold flour at catalogue price and wait indefinitely; assume that valuation pays for meals. No actual sale.
options.c: Sell a measured load of my flour to the known funded bakery at a margin, return the operating share to the mill and draw only surplus for meals. Preserves working capital; restores spendable cash.
